roadmap.notes:
OPERATING MODEL: 22 acceptance scenarios (ca01-ca05, per direct read of tests/client_auth/acceptance/*.rs -- ca01=6, ca02=7, ca03=4, ca04=4, ca05=1) plus 14 layer-1 unit/property tests in crates/embyr-core/src/client_identity/mod.rs (inline #[cfg(test)], run via `cargo test -p embyr-core`) plus 3 already-GREEN pure-routing unit tests in crates/embyr-server/src/grpc/handler.rs::client_identity_extension_tests (legitimate GREEN-by-construction per docs/feature/client-auth/distill/red-classification.md -- not RED, not touched by this roadmap). For each step below, un-ignore the scenario(s) named in scenario_name ONE AT A TIME (ca01's WS scenario and ca02's WS scenario are the two already non-#[ignore] RED scenarios; every other listed scenario is #[ignore]), implement just enough of the named production symbol(s) to make it pass, then run the FULL ca01..ca05 suite (not just the one test) plus `cargo test -p embyr-core client_identity` before committing -- ca03/ca04 scenarios reuse ca02's sign-in endpoint and 01-01's shared verify function, so a regression there is cheap to catch immediately. AC-16-08(a) full-72-scenario-suite regression command (ADR-026 Enforcement, feature-delta.md DISTILL Pre-DELIVER Gate) must be re-run after 02-02 lands, not only once at the end.

GROUPING RATIONALE: (1) 01-01 bundles BOTH pure functions in crates/embyr-core/src/client_identity/mod.rs (verify_client_identity_token AND credential_fingerprint) plus their full 14-test suite into one step, even though credential_fingerprint's only caller in this feature is registration (US-01) and verify_client_identity_token's callers are sign-in/rotate/debug-verify (US-02/03/04, later steps) -- both functions live in the same file, share the same RED-scaffold table row in DISTILL, and the 14-test suite already exercises both together (fingerprint determinism, all 4 rejection reasons, algorithm-confusion, signature-before-claims ordering, ADR-025 rotation-window trial order, 3 proptest! properties). Splitting them would mean touching the same file twice for no implementation-risk reduction. This mirrors customer-db-onboarding's step 03-01 (pure fn + proptest suite + its first real I/O caller as one step) -- here the 'first real I/O caller' is the registration handler (ca01, Activity A, earliest in the DISCUSS Story Map), with verify_client_identity_token's own real callers following in 02-01/02-02/03-01/04-01, all of which the critical-dependency instruction requires to come strictly after 01-01. (2) ca05 (algorithm-confusion regression) is folded into 02-01, NOT given its own step, per this task's explicit instruction: it exercises the identical REST sign-in endpoint and the identical verify_client_identity_token algorithm-pinning logic as ca02's other 5 scenarios -- it is a property of one implementation unit, not a second one. (3) ca02's 7 scenarios are split across 02-01 (5: the WS sign-in scenario + all 4 AC-16-07 rejection-reason scenarios, all hitting rest/sign_in.rs) and 02-02 (2: the AC-16-08(b)/(c) guardrail scenarios, which hit a DIFFERENT file/call-site -- crates/embyr-server/src/grpc/handler.rs's authenticate() extension, not the REST sign-in handler) -- these are two distinct production call sites sharing the same underlying pure verify function from 01-01, so splitting them is the honest implementation-unit boundary, not an arbitrary scenario-count split. (4) 03-01 (rotate, all 4 ca03 scenarios) and 04-01 (debug-verify, all 4 ca04 scenarios) are each one implementation unit -- one new admin handler + (for 03-01 only) one new system_db mutation method -- with no internal sub-grouping warranted, matching DISTILL's own file-level scaffold boundaries.

STEP COUNT: 5 (vs. an implicit 5-file 1:1 split if ca02 were kept as one 7-scenario step and ca05 given its own step, which this task's dispatch instructions explicitly forbid) -- decomposition ratio 5 steps / 6 production files (crates/embyr-core/src/client_identity/mod.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/adapters/system_db.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/client_identity.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/shared.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/rest/sign_in.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/grpc/handler.rs) = 0.83, well under the 2.5 ceiling. Max scenarios in any single step is 6 (01-01 and 02-01, tied), under the 8-scenario flag threshold -- no step flagged. Composition-root plumbing (Cargo.toml x3, migrations/0021_client_identity_credentials.sql, admin/router.rs's 3 new session_router routes, rest/mod.rs's pub mod sign_in, embyr-core/src/lib.rs's pub mod client_identity, embyr-server::spawn_all_servers's REST-router merge) is already real, wired code per DISTILL's Scaffolds table -- it is NOT listed in any step's files_to_modify and NO step needs to touch it.

FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE (done before assignment, per this dispatch's explicit instruction -- traced against the actual ctx.seed_credential()/ctx.seed_session() calls in tests/client_auth/common/mod.rs and the acceptance files themselves, not assumed from the DISCUSS/DESIGN narrative alone): ca02, ca03, and ca04 all hand-seed their client_identity_credentials row DIRECTLY via ClientAuthAdminContext::seed_credential()/ClientAuthFullContext::seed_credential() (raw SQL INSERT, bypassing the register HTTP endpoint entirely) -- confirmed by reading every scenario body. This means, contrary to a surface reading of the DISCUSS/DESIGN narrative, NONE of ca02/ca03/ca04's own acceptance scenarios actually require the US-01 registration HANDLER (crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/client_identity.rs::register_client_identity_credential) to be implemented first -- only crates/embyr-core/src/client_identity/mod.rs's pure verify_client_identity_token() (01-01) is a genuine cross-cutting prerequisite for 02-01/02-02/03-01/04-01, exactly as this task's own 'Critical dependency to get right' section states. 01-01 nonetheless implements the registration handler alongside the pure module (see Grouping Rationale (1) above) because it is that pure module's natural first real caller and completes US-01/Slice-01 end-to-end in one step -- not because a later step's tests require it. 02-01 additionally implements system_db::get_client_identity_credential (new read method) because rest/sign_in.rs needs it to load the row seeded directly by ca02's own fixtures; 03-01 and 04-01 both REUSE that same read method (03-01 also adds a new WRITE method, rotate_client_identity_credential; 04-01 adds no new system_db method at all -- debug-verify only reads). 02-02 (the AC-16-08 guardrail, grpc/handler.rs's authenticate() extension) depends ONLY on 01-01, not on 02-01 -- confirmed by reading both AC-16-08(b) (needs verify_client_identity_token directly, already real via 01-01) and AC-16-08(c) (needs no credential row and no verify call at all, since the header is absent -- it is a pure structural-unreachability proof). 02-02 is listed with dependencies:['01-01'] only, deliberately NOT ['02-01'], even though implementing it after 02-01 is the natural build order -- this is a documented, verified independence, not an oversight. 03-01's dependency on 02-01 (not just 01-01) is real: ca03's own scenarios call POST .../accounts:signInWithCustomToken (rest/sign_in.rs, built in 02-01) to empirically prove the rotation window, so 02-01 must exist first even though 03-01's OWN production code (the rotate handler + system_db mutation) does not itself call sign_in.rs's code.

PBT NOTE: 01-01 is this feature's one PBT-appropriate surface (embyr-core::client_identity's 3 proptest! properties -- claims round-trip, past-expiry always rejected, project-mismatch always rejected, 64 cases each, already specified by DISTILL) -- flagged in its own implementation_notes, using Rust's `proptest` (this project's Hypothesis-equivalent, already a workspace dev-dependency) per CLAUDE.md's functional-where-practical Rust paradigm, not a literal Hypothesis translation. Every other step (02-01, 02-02, 03-01, 04-01) is layer-3 acceptance-level (real HTTP/gRPC + real testcontainers Postgres, verifying wiring through a real driving port) and is EXEMPT per Mandate 9 -- each step's implementation_notes states the exemption individually. Mutation gate (per-feature, per project CLAUDE.md): `cargo-mutants -p embyr-core --filter client_identity` (ADR-024 Enforcement) targets 01-01's pure verification/fingerprint logic specifically, run once 01-01 is GREEN.

EARNED TRUST NOTE: DESIGN (feature-delta.md § Driven Ports + Adapters -- client-auth) already concluded, with explicit reasoning, that NO new probe() is required anywhere in this feature -- no new substrate dependency is introduced (verify_client_identity_token's only 'environment' is CPU-deterministic Ed25519 signature math; the existing SystemDb driven port is reused unchanged for the new table, inheriting whatever probe SystemDb already has, unmodified). This roadmap does not re-litigate that conclusion or add a probe() anywhere; no step below introduces a new driven adapter.

OPEN QUESTION FLAG (non-blocking): OQ-CA-01 (feature-delta.md § DESIGN Open Questions -- exact signInWithCustomToken() wire fidelity against the real Firebase JS SDK) remains an unresolved empirical spike, explicitly deferred past DISTILL. This roadmap implements ADR-026's best-evidence transport assumption (new x-embyr-client-identity header/metadata key, new REST endpoint) as specified -- it does not attempt the spike. If the spike (separate, DELIVER-adjacent work) later disproves the header assumption, 02-01 (rest/sign_in.rs) and 02-02 (grpc/handler.rs's header extraction) are the two call sites to revise per ADR-026's own documented dual_auth-style fallback; crates/embyr-core/src/client_identity/mod.rs's pure contract (01-01) does not change either way.

REUSE-DEBT RESOLUTION: DISTILL flagged that admin/handlers/client_identity.rs::verify_project_ownership is currently a local copy of sdk_keys.rs's identical private helper, kept local during DISTILL to avoid touching already-green production code mid-acceptance-test-authoring. 01-01 performs the promotion to admin/handlers/shared.rs (mechanical, zero behavior change) as part of standing up the registration handler, so every later admin handler (03-01, 04-01) calls the promoted shared helper from day one rather than adding a third local copy.

RELEASE GROUPING: phases 01-02 (steps 01-01, 02-01, 02-02) = Release 1 / Walking Skeleton (US-01, US-02) -- outcome: any Trailmark end user can be verifiably identified end-to-end. Phases 03-04 (steps 03-01, 04-01) = Release 2 (US-03, US-04) -- outcome: Alex can operate the credential safely over time. This mirrors feature-delta.md's own Release 1/Release 2 split; no step crosses a release boundary.

phases.name: US-01: Alex Registers Trailmark's Verification Credential (Slice 01, Walking Skeleton Activity A, Release 1)

steps.name: Walking Skeleton (US-01) -- embyr-core::client_identity pure module (verify_client_identity_token + credential_fingerprint + 14 unit/property tests, ADR-024/025) + credential registration admin handler
criteria: A project with no verification credential registered yet accepts a well-formed 32-byte Ed25519 public key from an Owner/Admin session, returns 201, and the credential is stored and active (AC-16-01, walking skeleton)
The registration response never contains the raw public key material anywhere in its body, under any field name, in any successful or error response (AC-16-01)
Verification material that is not exactly 32 bytes is rejected with 400, naming specifically what is wrong (not a generic parse error) (AC-16-02)
A registration request with no session cookie, or a garbage/expired one, is rejected 401, identically to how any other admin endpoint rejects missing/invalid session credentials (AC-16-03)

A second registration attempt for a project that already has an active credential is rejected 409, and the response body directs the caller to the rotation action rather than silently overwriting or silently failing (AC-16-04)
A registration attempt against a project ID that does not exist (or was deleted) is rejected 404 (AC-16-05)
A session with the Viewer role (not Owner/Admin) cannot register a credential -- rejected 403, mirroring the existing sdk_keys.rs Owner/Admin-only precedent

verify_client_identity_token(): a token signed with the registered current key and unexpired verifies successfully; a token with no valid signature under either tracked key is rejected (Malformed); an otherwise-valid but past-expiry token is rejected (Expired); an otherwise-valid token whose aud does not match the project being checked is rejected (ProjectMismatch); signature validity is always checked BEFORE expiry/audience are trusted -- an attacker-forged token with an invalid signature and an arbitrary aud/exp must report Malformed, never Expired or ProjectMismatch; an alg:HS256 token forged using the registered public key's raw bytes as an HMAC secret is rejected as Malformed, never accepted (ADR-024 algorithm-confusion defense, layer-1 proof paired with the layer-2 proof in 02-01/ca05)
credential_fingerprint(): deterministic BLAKE3-truncated (16 hex char) fingerprint of a 32-byte public key, matching the dc_<16hex> NOTIFY-channel-naming truncation-length precedent

3 proptest! properties (64 cases each) hold across the input space: claims round-trip through mint/verify unchanged; any past-expiry timestamp is always rejected as Expired; any aud mismatch is always rejected as ProjectMismatch
steps.implementation_notes: Replace RED panics. crates/embyr-core/src/client_identity/mod.rs (per red-classification.md: 14/14 tests panic unconditionally today): verify_client_identity_token(token: &str, credential: &ClientIdentityCredential, expected_project_id: &str) -> Result<VerifiedEndUserIdentity, ClientIdentityVerifyError> -- use jsonwebtoken::decode with Validation::new(Algorithm::EdDSA) and an explicit single-element algorithms list (ADR-024: the verifier must be strictly single-algorithm; do not construct a Validation that accepts a broader algorithm set -- a token whose header alg is anything other than EdDSA, including HS256 forged from the public key's raw bytes, must fail decode() and map to Malformed). Try public_key_current first via DecodingKey::from_ed_der/from_bytes; on InvalidSignature specifically (not on other error kinds), retry against public_key_previous if Some (ADR-025 current-then-previous trial order) -- if both fail, or previous is None, map to Malformed. Map jsonwebtoken::ErrorKind per ADR-024's table: InvalidToken/Base64/Json/InvalidSignature/InvalidAlgorithm -> Malformed; ExpiredSignature -> Expired; InvalidAudience -> ProjectMismatch. 'Missing token' is explicitly out of this function's scope (ADR-024: 'checked before calling decode()') -- the caller (02-01's sign-in handler) checks for token presence before ever calling this function; do not add a Missing variant path here beyond what the existing ClientIdentityVerifyError enum already declares. credential_fingerprint(public_key: &[u8; 32]) -> String -- blake3::hash(public_key), take the first 8 bytes, hex-encode (16 hex chars), matching the dc_<16hex>-truncation-length precedent (crates/embyr-core's existing NOTIFY-channel-naming code). Write all 14 tests per DISTILL's Scenario List row (4 rejection reasons, algorithm-confusion HS256-forgery, signature-before-claims-trusted ordering, ADR-025 rotation-window trial order across current-only/current+previous/both-fail, 3 proptest! properties at 64 cases each per PBT NOTE in the roadmap-level notes, fingerprint determinism). crates/embyr-server/src/adapters/system_db.rs: add ClientIdentityCredentialRow struct + insert_client_identity_credential(project_id: &str, public_key: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<ClientIdentityCredentialRow, sqlx::Error> issuing 'INSERT INTO client_identity_credentials (project_id, public_key_current, algorithm) VALUES ($1, $2, 'EdDSA') RETURNING *' -- map the Postgres unique-violation (SQLSTATE 23505, the PRIMARY KEY on project_id per ADR-025) to a distinguishable error variant the handler translates to 409; do NOT implement get_client_identity_credential or rotate_client_identity_credential in this step (see FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE in the roadmap-level notes -- they belong to 02-01/03-01, whose own scenarios are what require them). crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/shared.rs (new file, promotion target): move verify_project_ownership out of sdk_keys.rs's private copy into a pub(crate) fn here with an identical signature; update sdk_keys.rs's own call site to use the promoted version (mechanical, zero behavior change -- DISTILL's own documented reuse-debt flag). crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/client_identity.rs: register_client_identity_credential handler -- session-auth (reuses existing SessionContext extractor, ADR-009/010, zero new middleware), Owner/Admin role gate mirroring sdk_keys.rs::create_sdk_key exactly, calls the promoted verify_project_ownership (404 if the project doesn't exist or isn't owned by the caller's account), decodes the request body's base64url public_key field and rejects (400, naming the byte count found vs. the required 32) if the decoded length is not exactly 32, calls insert_client_identity_credential, maps the unique-violation case to 409 with a response body containing the substring 'rotat' (ca01's own assertion), and on success returns 201 with {project_id, algorithm: 'EdDSA', fingerprint: credential_fingerprint(key), created_at} -- construct this response type explicitly (do not #[derive(Serialize)] on any struct that also holds the raw key bytes; a field that is never populated is safer than a field marked #[serde(skip)] on a struct that does hold it). TEST PARADIGM: crates/embyr-core/src/client_identity/mod.rs's own test suite IS this feature's property-based-test surface -- 3 proptest! properties over the claims/expiry/audience input space, at 64 cases each, matching the project's Rust-native equivalent of the generic Hypothesis-@given mandate (CLAUDE.md: functional-where-practical Rust paradigm; proptest is this workspace's already-present PBT tool). The 6 ca01 acceptance scenarios in this same step remain layer-3/example-based and are EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: they verify real HTTP + real Postgres wiring through the admin driving port, not the pure verification/fingerprint invariants, which the proptest suite above covers directly.

phases.name: US-02: A Trailmark User's Verified Identity Unlocks Their Firestore Session (Slice 02, Walking Skeleton Activity B, Release 1)

steps.name: Walking Skeleton (US-02) -- REST sign-in handler (signInWithCustomToken) calling the shared verify function, all 4 rejection reasons, and the ADR-024 algorithm-confusion regression
criteria: A session presenting a valid, current-project, unexpired token signs in successfully (200) and the response reports the resolved end-user identity and a positive expires-in duration (AC-16-06, walking skeleton)
Signing in with no token present is rejected 400 with a reason identifying the missing token, distinguishable from every other rejection reason (AC-16-07)
Signing in with a structurally corrupted/malformed token is rejected 400 with a reason distinguishable from the missing-token reason (AC-16-07)
Signing in with a token that is otherwise valid but past its expiry is rejected 400 with a reason identifying expiry, distinguishable from malformed or missing (AC-16-07)

Signing in with a token minted for a different project than the one being signed into is rejected 400 with a reason identifying the project mismatch, distinguishable from the other three reasons (AC-16-07)

A token forged with alg:HS256 using the registered project's PUBLIC key bytes as the HMAC secret is rejected 400 with the identical 'malformed' reason a structurally-corrupted token receives -- never accepted as a successful sign-in, and never reported as any reason other than malformed (ADR-024 algorithm-confusion defense, layer-2 acceptance-level proof)
steps.implementation_notes: Replace the RED panic in crates/embyr-server/src/rest/sign_in.rs::sign_in_with_custom_token (per red-classification.md: surfaces as HTTP 500 today). Handler shape: POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/accounts:signInWithCustomToken, body {token: Option<String>} (missing/absent field, not just empty string, is the MISSING_TOKEN case -- ca02's sign_in() test helper sends an empty JSON object `{}` for this case, confirm serde's Option<String> default-missing deserialization handles it without a custom deserializer). If token is None -> 400 {"reason": "MISSING_TOKEN"} without ever loading a credential row or calling verify_client_identity_token (mirrors ADR-024's 'checked before calling decode()' contract from 01-01). Otherwise call the new system_db::get_client_identity_credential(project_id) -> Option<ClientIdentityCredentialRow> (SELECT project_id, public_key_current, public_key_previous, algorithm FROM client_identity_credentials WHERE project_id = $1 -- add this method now; 03-01 and 04-01 both reuse it unchanged, and it must select BOTH public_key columns since 01-01's verify_client_identity_token already implements the current-then-previous trial internally and expects both). If no credential row exists for the project, treat identically to Malformed for sign-in purposes (no acceptance scenario in this step exercises this exact case for sign-in specifically, but the handler must not panic or 500 -- return the same 400/MALFORMED_TOKEN shape rather than inventing a fifth reason). Otherwise call embyr_core::client_identity::verify_client_identity_token(token, &credential, project_id) (01-01, now real) and map its Result per ADR-026's table: Ok(identity) -> 200 {"localId": identity.end_user_id, "expiresIn": seconds_until(identity.exp)}; Err(Malformed) -> 400 {"reason": "MALFORMED_TOKEN"}; Err(Expired) -> 400 {"reason": "TOKEN_EXPIRED"}; Err(ProjectMismatch) -> 400 {"reason": "PROJECT_MISMATCH"}. The ca05 algorithm-confusion scenario requires NO handler-side branching beyond what's already here -- an alg:HS256 forged token fails jsonwebtoken::decode() inside 01-01's verify_client_identity_token with an algorithm-mismatch error, which 01-01 already maps to ClientIdentityVerifyError::Malformed; this step's only job is to make sure that Err variant reaches the wire as reason:'MALFORMED_TOKEN' exactly like any other malformed token, proving there is no separate, weaker code path for the algorithm-confusion case. Do not implement anything in crates/embyr-server/src/grpc/handler.rs in this step -- the AC-16-08 guardrail scenarios are a separate implementation unit, see 02-02. TEST PARADIGM: all 6 scenarios in this step are layer-3 acceptance tests (real REST HTTP via reqwest against embyr_server::start_test_server's actual REST port, real testcontainers Postgres, real Ed25519/HS256 token minting in tests/client_auth/common/mod.rs -- Pillar 3, zero mocked driving port). EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: these verify real end-to-end wiring through the new driving port, not the pure verify_client_identity_token invariants -- 01-01's proptest suite already covers those directly; adding a second PBT layer here at the HTTP-integration level would explore the identical bounded 4-reason taxonomy a second time at far higher per-case cost for no new contract-gap discovery (mirrors DISTILL's own Two-Tier Acceptance Composition Decision reasoning for this feature).

steps.name: authenticate() gRPC extension -- additive, structurally-unreachable-without-the-header client-identity attach step (AC-16-08 regression guardrail)
criteria: A request carrying a valid api_key and an EXPIRED x-embyr-client-identity token succeeds on an ordinary getDoc call exactly as it would with no client-identity header at all -- an expired or otherwise-invalid identity token attached to a data-plane call never turns a previously-working call into a failure (AC-16-08(b))

A request carrying a valid api_key and NO x-embyr-client-identity header at all succeeds on an ordinary getDoc call, and the new client-identity verification logic is never invoked for that request -- not merely unobserved, but structurally unreachable, since the new step is gated entirely on the header's presence (AC-16-08(c))

This step introduces no change to the existing three-role api_key check's happy path, error surface, or ordering -- the new logic is appended strictly after step 3 of the existing authenticate() function completes exactly as it does today
steps.implementation_notes: Replace the RED panic path in crates/embyr-server/src/grpc/handler.rs::authenticate()'s new step 4 (per red-classification.md: 'calls into the embyr-core scaffold when the header IS present' -- the header-absent branch and extract_client_identity_token's metadata-parsing are already real, non-scaffold code per Mandate 7's routing-vs-business-logic distinction, confirmed GREEN by the 3 existing client_identity_extension_tests). Per ADR-026's exact decision shape: after the existing unchanged steps 1-3 (api_key extraction/Argon2id verify, rate limit, AdapterForProject) complete, check whether extract_client_identity_token(metadata) returned Some(token) (already-real routing). If None, attach nothing and proceed -- UNCHANGED behavior, this branch requires no new code, only confirms 02-01's sibling embyr-core module is never called (proven by AC-16-08(c) passing: if this branch were reachable without the header it would call the 01-01 scaffold's real implementation over a nonexistent credential row and either error cleanly or attach an identity, either of which would NOT match the test's 'not seeding a credential row at all, request must still succeed exactly as an unrelated call' assertion in a way that reveals the branch was entered). If Some(token): load the project's client_identity_credentials row via system_db::get_client_identity_credential (02-01, already real by the time this step lands) using the SAME project_id already resolved in step 1; call embyr_core::client_identity::verify_client_identity_token(token, &credential, project_id) (01-01, already real); on Ok(identity) attach VerifiedEndUserIdentity to the request's extension/context (exact carrier type is an internal decision -- e.g. tonic::Request extensions or a request-scoped struct threaded to the RPC handler -- no acceptance scenario in this feature asserts on the internal representation, only on 'the underlying getDoc call still succeeds', consistent with AC-16-09's DESIGN-deferred exposure mechanism); on Err(_) of ANY variant (Malformed/Expired/ProjectMismatch -- Missing is not reachable here since step 4 is only entered when extract_client_identity_token returned Some) attach nothing and DO NOT reject the request -- proceed to the RPC handler exactly as if the header had been absent. This failure-does-not-reject behavior is the load-bearing property AC-16-08(b) tests directly. Per DISTILL's own scope limitation (explicitly flagged, not a gap in this step): wire this new step 4 into handle_get_document only in this step, matching the only RPC method any acceptance scenario in this DISTILL run exercises -- wiring the identical additive call into the other 8 RPC methods (BatchGetDocuments, RunQuery, CreateDocument, UpdateDocument, DeleteDocument, BeginTransaction, Commit, Listen) is explicit follow-through for a later DELIVER pass, not required by any scenario in this roadmap; do not silently expand scope to all 9 RPCs in this step. Re-run the full existing 72-scenario embyr-rs acceptance suite (command in feature-delta.md DISTILL Pre-DELIVER Gate / ca02's own module doc comment) after this step lands, asserting 0 regressions -- this operationalizes KPI #3 and ADR-026's own Enforcement section; do not defer this run to the end of the roadmap. TEST PARADIGM: both scenarios are layer-3 acceptance/integration tests (real gRPC client against embyr_server::start_test_server's actual gRPC port, real testcontainers Postgres) verifying a structural wiring property (unreachability, non-rejection), not a data-space invariant. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: there is no pure-function input space here to property-test -- the guarantee is about CODE REACHABILITY (a branch either is or isn't entered), which a property-based test over generated inputs cannot express more directly than this pair of pointed examples already does; the adjacent pure-function invariants (rejection-reason correctness) are already covered by 01-01's proptest suite.

phases.name: US-03: Alex Rotates Trailmark's Verification Credential Without Breaking Signed-In Users (Slice 03, Release 2)

steps.name: Credential rotation -- system_db rotate mutation + admin rotate handler, dual-generation window
criteria: A valid rotation request from an Owner/Admin session activates a new credential; a token freshly minted under that new credential verifies successfully via sign-in immediately afterward (AC-16-10)

A token minted under the credential that was active immediately before a rotation continues to verify successfully via sign-in after that rotation (the rotation window covers exactly one prior generation) (AC-16-11)

A token minted under a credential from TWO rotations ago (no longer current, no longer the immediately-previous generation) is rejected via sign-in with the same 'malformed/no-longer-valid' reason an ordinary invalid-signature token receives -- there is no separate 'stale credential' rejection class (AC-16-12)
A rotation request with no valid admin session is rejected 401, identically to how registration rejects the same condition (AC-16-13)
steps.implementation_notes: Replace the RED panic in crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/client_identity.rs::rotate_client_identity_credential (per red-classification.md: 3 of 4 ca03 scenarios panic inside this scaffold; the 4th, rotation_without_a_valid_session_is_rejected, is ALREADY PASSING today -- legitimate GREEN-by-construction, because session_auth_middleware, existing reused code, rejects the unauthenticated request before this handler is ever reached.
